vehicle.displayName: 2004 Ford Explorer Sport Trac — Repair Realm

parts.aftermarketPartNumber: CAPA-compatible equivalent — verify trim and paint code
replacementSteps: Disconnect the negative battery terminal and support the damaged bumper cover.
Remove grille, wheel-well fasteners, lower retainers, and any lamp or sensor connectors.
Transfer reusable energy absorber, lamps, brackets, and hardware after inspecting for hidden damage.
Install the replacement cover loosely, align panel gaps, then torque retainers to the service-manual specification.
parts.mentorScript: Start with support and safety. Hidden bumper damage is common, so inspect the reinforcement and mounting brackets before installing a new cover.

parts.partName: Front Left Wheel, Tire, and Brake Inspection Zone
parts.oemPartNumber: Wheel application varies by trim — verify wheel diameter and bolt pattern
parts.aftermarketPartNumber: Use a tire-and-wheel fitment catalog matched to 2004 Sport Trac trim
replacementSteps: Chock the rear wheels, raise the vehicle at the approved front lifting point, and support it with a rated stand.
Remove the wheel and inspect tire sidewall, rim runout, brake hose routing, and suspension hardware.
Replace damaged components one system at a time; do not reuse compromised lug hardware.
Install the wheel, lower the vehicle, and torque lug nuts in a star pattern to the current service-manual specification.
parts.mentorScript: A wheel-zone impact can move more than the wheel itself. Check brake lines, steering links, and suspension mounting points before treating this as a tire-only repair.

parts.oemPartNumber: Door shell varies by paint code, trim, and power-option package
parts.aftermarketPartNumber: Use a corrosion-protected shell; transfer compatible internal hardware after inspection
replacementSteps: Disconnect battery power before opening harness connectors or working around side-impact wiring.
Support the door with a stand, mark hinge positions, and disconnect the harness through the body-side boot.
Transfer glass, regulator, latch, weather seals, and trim only after inspecting each part for collision damage.
Align the door for even gaps, verify latch engagement and weather sealing, then complete window and lock checks.
parts.mentorScript: Door alignment is a measurement job, not a force job. Stabilize the door, preserve hinge reference marks, and verify both latch engagement and window sealing before calling it finished.

parts.oemPartNumber: Verify engine code and emissions calibration before ordering engine-specific parts
replacementSteps: Allow the engine to cool fully and disconnect the negative battery cable before inspection.
Document fluid leaks, damaged mounts, broken accessories, and harness routing before removing parts.
Follow the workshop manual for the exact component procedure, torque sequence, and replacement seals.
After reassembly, verify fluid levels, check for leaks, and perform the required diagnostic and road-test checks.
parts.mentorScript: Use the engine bay as a system map. Before replacing any part, document what the impact moved, pinched, cracked, or contaminated. That prevents a quick repair from becoming a repeat repair.

parts.partName: Rear Bumper and Step Pad Assembly
parts.oemPartNumber: Verify bumper configuration, hitch package, and sensor cutouts before ordering
parts.aftermarketPartNumber: Use a corrosion-protected assembly with documented fitment
replacementSteps: Support the bumper and disconnect trailer, lamp, or sensor wiring as equipped.
Remove fasteners in sequence and inspect bumper brackets, frame attachment points, and harness retainers.
Install the replacement assembly loosely, center it to the body, then torque fasteners to service-manual specification.
Verify lamps, trailer connector operation, and tailgate clearance before returning the truck to service.
parts.mentorScript: Rear repairs hide damage behind the cover. Check brackets, frame attachment points, and trailer wiring before a new bumper makes the outside look finished.
